- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential reversal.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day); cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 days.  
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price moving toward historical mean), reduce forecast slope; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.4, -0.6, +0.3), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment’s 3-day moving average.
